access_links.label: Paper: An integrated model of traffic, geography and economy in the Internet

dedupe_keys.name: asim agent based model of traffic geography and economy in the autonomous system level internet

description: This paper presents ASIM (AS Simulation Model), a discrete agent-based model of Internet growth that integrates network structure, traffic flow, geography and economy, which earlier models treated separately. Each agent is an economic actor comparable to an Autonomous System, managing a geographically extended sub-network, profiting from the traffic that flows through it, upgrading its capacity and creating links to other ASes over time; the model adds explicit cost, population density and simplified traffic flow, and assumes agents never merge or go bankrupt. The authors characterise the time evolution, network topology, correlation between structure and traffic, packet routing statistics and geographic aspects, and show that the generated networks have topologies, dynamics and, more speculatively, spatial distributions similar to the Internet, comparing several topological measures with observed data. Producer: Holme (KTH and University of New Mexico), Karlin and Forrest (University of New Mexico and Santa Fe Institute). Coverage: a conceptual AS-level Internet. Access: the paper as a PDF; no code link was seen. Licence and cost: free to read, licence not stated. Caveats: the paper is dated and the mapping between agents and real ASes is admittedly inexact. Simulation uses: exploring how economics and traffic shape Internet topology and resilience at the AS level. Related record: the Peering Simulation Game (model-peering-simulation-game), a teaching model of peering negotiation.
